day.text: Blair, the Eagle gains from visitors to its target, which was Casey, not from visitors to the Eagle. Your Owl visit would have paid Alex, and it didn't. I'm voting Blair.
day.note: Blair misstated the Eagle rule, and Alex has it right. Blair's Owl visit to Casey would have given Alex an egg, so Blair's claim fails. Voting Blair.

day.text: Alex, the Eagle gains from visitors to the Eagle, not to its target, so your rule is wrong. My Owl report lists the Eagle visiting Casey, which is you. I'm throwing at Alex. Let's vote.
day.note: Alex is misstating the Eagle rule. Eagles gain from visitors to themselves, not to their target, so Alex's line that my Owl visit didn't happen is false. I'll call for the vote and throw at Alex.

day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.

Alex.note: Casey has been the most questioned player, and visiting them shows who visited them. The Eagle gains an egg for each visitor, so this is a useful check.

Blair.note: As the Owl I visit a player to see who visited them. Casey has been the most suspicious, so I'll check Casey.

Casey.note: As the Hawk I want to test a suspicious player. Finley kept accusing me and may be Meowfia, so I'll visit Finley.

Drew.note: I'm the Floofer, Meowfia. Alex leads the scores at 12, so I'll visit and hug Alex to shut down their night role.

Ellis.note: I'm Farm as the Kookaburra. Finley's Eagle claim conflicted with the nest last round, so I'll check Finley's role.

Alex.feeling: Tense and muddled: my Eagle nest contradicts Blair's Owl story, but Blair and Drew are pushing back on the Eagle rule, so the table is split on who to trust.

Blair.feeling: Round 3 is messy: Alex's Eagle story conflicts with my Owl report, and the table is split on whether to throw at Alex or me.

Casey.feeling: Tense and muddled: the Owl and Eagle stories about my nest conflict, and I can't verify either one from my own dawn reports.

Drew.feeling: Messy and contradictory: the Owl and Eagle stories don't reconcile, and I'm Meowfia myself, so I'm trying to steer suspicion without being seen as the one pushing.

Ellis.feeling: Messy: the Owl and Eagle stories about Casey contradict each other, and the table is split between throwing at Blair and Alex.

Finley.feeling: Messy round: Blair's and Casey's stories contradict the nests, but Alex's Eagle story and the Turkey payouts make it hard to be sure who is lying.

Alex.note: Blair's Owl visit fails against my Eagle nest, and most of the table is throwing at Blair. I'll throw my two lowest cards, C3 and H6, to add votes while keeping my high cards.

Blair.note: Alex's Eagle rule is wrong and the Owl report shows the Eagle visiting Casey. I'll throw my lowest card at Alex.

Casey.note: Most of the table is throwing at Blair, and Blair's Owl story conflicts with Alex's Eagle. I'll throw two low cards at Blair to add votes.

Drew.note: Blair's Owl visit fits my hug on Alex, which makes Alex's no-visitor claim false, so Blair looks Farm. Throwing my Wild W3 (worth 0 if it banks) at Blair adds a vote without costing me points.

Ellis.note: I'm Farm and the table's consensus is on Blair, whose Owl story has the unexplained gap. I'll add a wild, which is zero value, so the risk is minimal.

Finley.note: Blair's Owl claim fails against Alex's nest and Casey's payouts, so I'm throwing at Blair. I'm using one mid-low card to keep my risk low.

Alex.confusing: The Eagle's visitor rule was easy to misstate in the day, and the Turkey payout timing (eggs gained from visitors only show up in the Turkey's own nest) took a while to pin down. Blair and I also disagreed on which nest a visit touches.
Alex.fun: Round 1 was satisfying: Casey's Pigeon claim collided with Finley's unchanged nest, and the table converged on Casey in a single caw.
Alex.change: I would make the day's nest-change reports include who visited whom, so visitor claims could be checked without relying on memory.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I threw at Blair too early and too heavily relative to the evidence; I should have asked Blair to explain their Owl report before calling caw, since my Eagle result was the only hard check and I didn't confirm it with Casey.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle's egg rule was easy to misread: it pays the Eagle for visitors to the Eagle, not to its target, and I misapplied it in round 3. That mix-up let Alex's false "no visitors" claim sound plausible.
Blair.fun: Round 1's Casey vote, where the Pigeon egg failed to appear in Finley's nest and the table caught the lie from nest counts alone. Cross-checking claims against egg changes felt like real deduction.
Blair.change: Make the dawn report list which visitors came to you, so Owl and Eagle claims can be checked without relying on memory and guesswork. The bare egg count left too much room for conflicting stories.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I threw at Alex on a misread of the Eagle rule and never checked Alex's claim against the Owl report I already had. I would have held off and asked Alex to explain the Eagle payout first.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle and Turkey payout rules were hard to track: it was unclear whether an Eagle gains from visits to its target or from visits it makes, and the reports alone didn't settle it.
Casey.fun: Round 1's Pigeon claim got challenged by the whole table, and the nest counts became the real evidence that decided who was lying.
Casey.change: Make dawn reports list visitors by animal so players can cross-check claims directly instead of arguing over who gained what.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I joined the throw at Blair instead of pushing harder on Alex's Eagle report, which was the claim that didn't fit the nests.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle's rule was the most confusing: it's unclear whether it gains eggs from visitors to its target or from visitors to itself. Several of us argued opposite readings all game, and the dawn reports didn't settle it.
Drew.fun: Round 3's Blair-versus-Alex fight, where the Owl and Eagle stories clashed and the table split, was the most fun. Watching the nest counts decide who was lying was satisfying.
Drew.change: I'd make the Eagle's rule explicit in the reports, since the nest-count arguments were built on different readings of it. I'd also make visit results clearer so people can check claims faster.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I made up a Kookaburra visit to Finley and then threw at Casey, a Farm player, so Farm won and I was eggsecuted. Instead I'd have stayed quiet, kept my nest, and avoided drawing attention to my own claim.

Ellis.confusing: The Eagle rule was hard to read: it was unclear whether an Eagle gains eggs from visitors to its target or to itself, and that confusion drove the Round 3 dispute.
Ellis.fun: Round 2, when Drew's Kookaburra visit was tested against Finley's unchanged nest, and the table converged on Drew and won the round.
Ellis.change: I would have dawn reports name each visitor when an egg is gained, so players could check claims against each other instead of arguing from counts.
Ellis.regret: In Round 3 I joined the throw at Blair without pressing Alex's Eagle claim, which was the story that actually contradicted the nests. I would have questioned Alex's no-visitor claim before backing the vote.

Finley.confusing: The Eagle's egg rule was easy to misread: several players, including me, argued about whether it pays for visits to the Eagle or to its target. That confusion decided the round 3 vote.
Finley.fun: Round 1 unraveled nicely: Casey's Pigeon claim said an egg went into my nest, and my unchanged count exposed the lie for the whole table.
Finley.change: I would have the Storyteller show each Eagle's visit target and visitor list in the public day report, so the egg-rule arguments could be settled from the table.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I threw at Blair, who was truly Farm, after trusting a shaky reading of the Eagle rule. I should have pressed Alex's Eagle claim against Casey's nest instead of joining the vote on Blair.

review.title: Eagle Rules Meltdown
review.headline: Two Farm players argued over Eagle rules and eggsecuted the real Owl.
review.summary: Round 1 and 2 ended with the table correctly eggsecuting a Meowfia, helped by nest-count contradictions and a clumsy fake Pigeon and fake Kookaburra. Round 3 broke down: Alex (Eagle) and Blair (Owl) both told the truth about their night, but misread how the Eagle scores, and the table threw at Blair. The lone Meowfia, Drew, hugged Alex, stayed quiet and won without being suspected. Alex finished first at 12 points, ahead of Finley on 10.

rounds.recap: Casey (Mouser) claimed Pigeon and said she laid an egg in Finley's nest, but Finley had gained nothing. Everyone piled on Casey and she was eggsecuted. Ellis, the other Meowfia, joined the throw and lost with her.

Drew (Mouser) claimed Kookaburra, and said he visited Finley the Eagle. Blair and Ellis argued this contradicted Finley's unchanged nest, using a wrong Eagle rule. Drew was eggsecuted anyway, since Casey, Blair, Alex and Ellis all aimed at him.

Drew (Floofer) hugged Alex, which stopped his Eagle's report from working as Alex believed. Alex and Blair both described the Eagle and Owl results honestly but each misread the Eagle rule. The table threw at Blair, a Farm player, so the lone Meowfia won.

highlights.text: Casey's Pigeon claim collapsed against Finley's +0 nest, a clean cross-check that ended the round fast.
Drew's Kookaburra cover story was ruined by the Eagle's nest count, though both sides misapplied the Eagle rule while arguing it.
Drew's hug on Alex turned an honest Eagle and an honest Owl into an apparent contradiction, and the Farm threw at the Owl.
Drew's only play was staying quiet, and he won the round with no suspicion on him.

confusions.what: Said nobody visited him as Turkey, then corrected: visitors are exactly who the Turkey pays.
Claimed the Owl learned nobody else visited Alex, but the Owl only learns the animals that visited.
Said the Eagle should gain an egg for visiting Drew, mixing up visits made with visits received.
Said the Eagle gains for visitors to the Eagle, so Drew's visit to Finley should have paid Finley. The Eagle gains for visitors to its target.
Repeated the same wrong Eagle rule against Drew.
Doubted Casey because a Turkey 'has to say who it visited', though the Turkey stays home.
Insisted the Eagle gains from visitors to itself, then used this to defend her Owl visit.
Said Casey having no visitors disproved the Owl's visit, ignoring that Blair is a visitor, not a gain-causing target. He also read his own Eagle gain after a hug as clean.
Said she gained no egg from visiting Finley, then claimed the +1 came from a visitor. She was Farm and had forgotten the Turkey payout.
Gave the Owl-Eagle chain muddled analysis, saying a visit doesn't give Casey an egg.

worked: Nest-size changes shown at the start of the day: they gave hard evidence (Finley +0 sank Casey's Pigeon in round 1).
Hug (Floofer): a quiet Meowfia night action that broke a Farm role's report and caused a believable contradiction in round 3.
Throwing low cards and Wilds as cheap votes: it made the throw decision a real risk-versus-reward choice.
problems: Eagle wording ('lay an egg for every visitor they had') is ambiguous, and four players misread it. Rewrite it as 'for every visitor to the player you visited'.
Hug and Owl/Eagle interactions are untransparent. Alex was told only 'no eggs', which looked identical to a clean no-visitor result. Add a dawn line like 'you were hugged'.
Only one Meowfia in round 3 meant no teammate to check or bluff against. A false contradiction decided the round, and a single quiet Meowfia was almost untouchable.
Round 1 and 2 votes ended fast on one nest-count mismatch, so little real deduction or bluffing was needed. Consider requiring more beats before CAW.
Rounds 1 and 2 had 7 or 8 claims that were mostly truthful and uninteresting, and nobody used the Wink at all. The Mouser's Wink never mattered, so give it a stronger trigger or reward.
